title: Read subscription periods and invoice subscription/paid where Stripe API 2025-03-31.basil puts them

export async function processStripeEvent(event: Stripe.Event) {
  switch (event.type) {

addresses.change: 2025-03-31.basil: Subscription.current_period_start/end moved to subscription items; Invoice.subscription moved to parent.subscription_details.subscription; Invoice.paid removed

reason: Webhook bodies are rendered at the webhook ENDPOINT's API version, not at the version the application's client declares. When the endpoint is on 2025-03-31.basil or later, the processor reads fields that no longer exist: every Subscription is stored with currentPeriodEnd null, and every Invoice with stripeSubscriptionId null and paid null — while the webhook answers 200, so nothing looks wrong.
originalBehavior: currentPeriodEnd = sub.current_period_end; stripeSubscriptionId = inv.subscription; paid = inv.paid (all undefined under basil, stored as null)
replacementBehavior: the same fields, taken from items.data[0].current_period_end, parent.subscription_details.subscription and status === 'paid' when the old field is absent; payloads that still carry the old fields are processed exactly as before
providerEvidence: https://docs.stripe.com/webhooks/versioning (webhook bodies use the endpoint's API version)
assumptions: A subscription has one item, or its items share one billing period (the application stores one period end per subscription). With items on different periods the first item's period is stored.
'paid' means the invoice status is 'paid' (Stripe's replacement for the removed boolean).
Events from earlier API versions still carry the old fields and are not changed.
validation: replay every recorded event at the earlier version through the original and the patched processor: identical records
replay every recorded basil event through the patched processor: records equal what Stripe states for the same objects
the webhook handler (signature check, idempotency, retries) is not changed
the original artifact still loads (rollback target)
rollback: Roll back the correction: the original artifact (unpatched processor) runs again; records written while it was active stay as written.
